issues.failure_explanation: The statement of Theorem thm:Phi_smooth asserts the pure Hölder bound ||∇F*(x) − ∇F*(x′)|| ≤ (1−θ)^{−1}C^{−1/θ}L_{∇f}^{1/θ}‖x−x′‖^{(1−θ)/θ}. The proof, however, only derives the two-term bound (eq. thm1_holder_bound1) ||∇F*(x) − ∇F*(x′)|| ≤ L_{∇f}‖x′−x‖ + (1−θ)^{−1}C^{−1/θ}L_{∇f}^{1/θ}‖x−x′‖^{(1−θ)/θ}, whose first (linear) term comes from the L_{∇f}-Lipschitz continuity of ∇_x f in x and is generically nonzero. The final line claims the stated display 'directly follow[s]' from this chain, but the linear term cannot be removed: the stated one-term inequality is strictly stronger than anything derived and is generically false (e.g., for inner problems of the form f(x,y)=s(xy−y²/2) on a long box, where ∇F*(x)=clip(x) varies linearly over the admissible ball while the claimed constant can be smaller). Thus the second display of the theorem is unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the linear term in display (thm1_HolderU), i.e., state ||∇F*(x) − ∇F*(x′)|| ≤ L_{∇f}‖x−x′‖ + (1−θ)^{−1}C^{−1/θ}L_{∇f}^{1/θ}‖x−x′‖^{(1−θ)/θ} (which the proof derives); on bounded subsets of U_ε this still yields a genuine local Hölder-smoothness statement with an adjusted constant, so the abstract/introductory claim of local Hölder smoothness survives.
issues.overall_effect: The second displayed inequality of Theorem thm:Phi_smooth (the advertised local Hölder-smoothness bound of F* with constant (1−θ)^{−1}C^{−1/θ}L_{∇f}^{1/θ}) is not established and is false as stated. Downstream results are not invalidated: the analysis in Section 4 (bounds Fstar-bound, the descent lemma in Lemma gen_converge, and the complexity theorems) uses exactly the corrected two-term bound with the linear term L_{∇f}‖x−x′‖ retained, so those proofs remain sound.
issues.title: Hölder bound in Theorem thm:Phi_smooth drops the linear term derived in its own proof
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line correction of the displayed inequality (reinstating the linear term, which the proof itself derives and which Section 4 already uses); the advertised property (local Hölder smoothness, with a rate and a constant of the same type) and all downstream guarantees survive unchanged, so no nontrivial new argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The notation subsection states the sum rule ∂(φ₁+φ₂)(x) = ∇φ₁(x) + ∂φ₂(x) under the hypothesis that φ₁ is merely differentiable; this is false — Clarke's sum rule requires φ₁ to be strictly differentiable (for φ₁(x)=x²sin(1/x), φ₂=0 one has ∂φ₁(0)=[−1,1] ≠ {∇φ₁(0)}). Lemma lem:open's proof invokes this equality ('∂Ψ = ∂F* + ∂p on X') at arbitrary points of C ⊆ X, where F* is only Lipschitz and differentiable merely almost everywhere (the proof itself invokes Rademacher), so neither the stated rule's hypothesis nor the equality is available at those points; the subsequent outer-semicontinuity deduction for ∂Ψ is therefore unsupported as written. The conclusion of the lemma remains true, and the same proof already establishes the missing hypothesis (∂^∞F*(z)={0}, i.e., local boundedness of ∂F*), which is exactly the constraint qualification under which the correct Clarke sum rule for a locally Lipschitz function plus a proper closed convex function holds.

issues.overall_effect: The written justification of Lemma lem:open (openness of U_ε, used to extend a.e. differentiability to all of U_ε in Theorem thm:Phi_smooth) rests on a misstated sum rule; as written the step is unjustified. The lemma's conclusion is nonetheless correct, because the constraint qualification ∂^∞F*(z)={0} verified in the preceding sentence makes the standard Clarke sum rule applicable, so no downstream result is invalidated.
issues.title: Clarke sum rule stated (and invoked) without the strict-differentiability hypothesis it requires
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local citation/hypothesis fix: the correct Clarke sum rule applies under the qualification the proof itself establishes one sentence earlier, so Lemma lem:open and all dependents (the differentiability part of Theorem thm:Phi_smooth and its uses) survive with no new argument or loss.
